name: cardano.nexus
title: cardano.nexus — A Place Where the Cardano Ecosystem Connects
description: A decentralised, permissionless connection layer for the Cardano ecosystem — a shared civic space where builders, projects, educators, SPOs, governance participants and communities discover each other and build trust over time. Grounded in the 4Cs: Curious · Caring · Constructive · Chill.
status_note: cardano.nexus is an open community proposal. The platform described here is not live yet: its Minimum Viable Version is the subject of a draft Cardano Treasury proposal. Describe features as proposed or planned unless a section says otherwise.

sections.title: Not a directory. Not a gatekeeper. A nexus.
sections.summary: Cardano already has the technical foundation. What's still emerging is the human, social and contextual layer that helps the ecosystem see itself clearly — and coordinate without becoming centralised.

items.name: A shared connective layer
items.desc: A layer the ecosystem can link itself together with.

items.name: A community-maintained graph of ecosystem context
items.desc: Checked, linked, improved.

items.name: Infrastructure you can trust without trusting a single owner
Part directory, part knowledge graph, part civic commons
Not the official voice of Cardano, or a central authority
Not a marketing directory or a popularity contest
Not a place where visibility is purchased
Not a platform that decides who belongs

sections.title: The 4Cs — the human operating model
sections.summary: Technology alone won't make the ecosystem coherent. The 4Cs are operating modes, each answering a different ecosystem need. Each mode balances the others.

items.name: Curious
items.desc: Discovery, learning and open questions. Curiosity prevents stagnation and makes space for new builders, ideas and collaborations — built into the information architecture through ecosystem maps, role-based pathways, 'start here' journeys and open research questions.

items.name: Caring
items.desc: Trust, stewardship and shared spaces. Care turns open participation into trusted participation: treating people as humans, not just wallets, votes or users — transparent histories, verifiable claims, anti-impersonation, recognition of invisible work.

items.name: Constructive
items.desc: Building, contributing and reducing friction. Cardano is built by contribution — technical, educational, social, operational, local. Constructiveness is measured by usefulness, not visibility.

items.name: Chill
items.desc: Sustainability, coherence and anti-burnout. Designing against urgency addiction, hype cycles and social exhaustion. Informed governance requires time, context and reflection — a frantic ecosystem cannot govern wisely.

items.name: Discover what exists
items.desc: Curiosity opens the ecosystem and keeps it learning.

items.name: Understand what can be trusted
items.desc: Caring humanises participation and protects shared spaces.

items.name: Contribute to what matters
items.desc: Constructiveness turns observation into shipped outcomes.

items.name: Sustain participation over time
items.desc: Chill keeps the ecosystem coherent as complexity grows.

sections.title: Seven connected layers
sections.summary: The proposed architecture: seven connected layers, each built on open standards, portable identity and interoperable data.

items.name: Identity
items.desc: People, projects, orgs, communities and tools represent themselves — with self-expression and verification, not a single forced identity model.

items.name: Context
items.desc: A shared graph of ecosystem knowledge — descriptions, dependencies, contributors, funding, roadmaps, relationships.

items.name: Contribution
items.desc: Makes useful work discoverable and recognisable — far more than code: docs, translations, events, governance rationales, maintenance.

items.name: Trust
items.desc: Represents trust without centralising authority. Plural and contextual: a dev trusted for code, a teacher for resources, a DRep for governance reasoning.

items.name: Governance
items.desc: Connects ecosystem participation with Cardano governance. It doesn't tell people how to vote — it helps them understand what they're voting on.

items.name: Learning
items.desc: Turns a complex ecosystem into a navigable one — beginner pathways, role-based onboarding, governance education, an ecosystem glossary.

items.name: API & Data
items.desc: Open, interoperable interfaces so others can build on top. Knowledge stays portable — it isn't trapped inside one platform.

sections.title: Design principles — built on Cardano's own values
sections.summary: A Cardano connection layer should inherit the values of Cardano itself — open participation, verifiable contribution, self-sovereign identity, community stewardship.

items.name: Permissionless
items.desc: Anyone can participate, create, connect and contribute.

items.name: Verifiable context
items.desc: Claims linked to evidence wherever possible.

items.name: Plural trust
items.desc: Trust is contextual — never one central rating.

items.name: Community stewardship
items.desc: Shared spaces get care, maintenance and transparent governance.

items.name: Open data
items.desc: The ecosystem graph stays portable and reusable.

items.name: Local autonomy
items.desc: Regional and thematic communities keep their own views.

items.name: Human-centred
items.desc: The platform serves people — it doesn't extract their attention.

items.name: Calm coordination
items.desc: Reduce noise, urgency and fragmentation.

items.name: Recognition
items.desc: Useful work becomes visible — including quiet, non-technical work.

items.name: Forkable & resilient
items.desc: No single operator can permanently capture shared context.

sections.title: The Verified Context Graph — ecosystem memory
sections.summary: Ecosystems forget — who contributed, why decisions were made, what was already tried. cardano.nexus proposes to help Cardano remember through linked, verifiable, community-maintained context. AI assists the ecosystem; it doesn't replace its judgement.

groups.title: Questions the graph is designed to answer

items.name: What projects are active in identity?
Which tools depend on which libraries?
Which governance debates shaped this decision?

sections.title: An open substrate for AI agents
sections.summary: cardano.nexus proposes to expose its Verified Context Graph to agents through an open A2A Protocol AgentCard, so agents assist the ecosystem instead of guessing about it. Read access is permissionless; agents assist discovery but never decide who belongs or how to vote. The five graph-backed skills below are planned for the MVP — today the agent files describe the proposal itself.

items.name: Ecosystem Discovery
items.desc: Find projects, people, tools, standards and communities. Who is building what, and where help is needed.
items.example: Which projects work on decentralised identity?

items.name: Governance Context
items.desc: Plain-language summaries, constitutional sections, DRep rationales and timelines. Never advises how to vote.
items.example: Summarise this governance action in plain terms.

items.name: Contribution Matching
items.desc: Surface open tasks, bounties and collaboration requests — recognising far more than code.
items.example: What open tasks match a Plutus developer?

items.name: Learning Pathways
items.desc: Role-based onboarding, beginner pathways, governance education and a navigable glossary.
items.example: I'm new to Cardano — where do I begin?

items.name: Context Graph Query
items.desc: Query ecosystem memory: dependencies, contributors, what funded a piece of work, the debates that shaped a decision.
items.example: Which tools depend on this library?

items.name: Discoverable
items.desc: A standard AgentCard at a standard path, no bespoke integration.

items.name: Verifiable
items.desc: Answers link back to signed claims and evidence in the graph.

items.name: Portable
items.desc: Open schemas mean knowledge is never trapped in one platform.

items.name: Bounded
items.desc: Agents assist discovery; they never decide who belongs or how to vote.

sections.title: How cardano.nexus governs itself
sections.summary: To serve a decentralised ecosystem, cardano.nexus should itself evolve toward decentralised governance. Start useful. Become trusted. Open the structure. Share the power.

items.name: Phase 1 — Stewarded Launch
items.desc: A small founding team establishes the initial platform, principles, schemas and prototype.

items.name: Phase 2 — Community Contribution
items.desc: Projects, communities and contributors begin adding profiles, context, resources and links.

items.name: Phase 3 — Stewardship Council
items.desc: A diverse stewardship group helps maintain quality, resolve disputes and guide evolution.

items.name: Phase 4 — Open Governance
items.desc: Governance mechanisms become more formal, transparent and community-driven.

items.name: Phase 5 — Protocolisation
items.desc: Core schemas, APIs and data structures become open standards that others can use, fork, mirror and extend.

sections.title: A useful first version (MVP)
sections.summary: The first version needs to create a useful place for connection. The early test: can someone arrive at cardano.nexus and understand the ecosystem better than before?

sections.title: Why governance needs context — on-chain power, off-chain confusion
sections.summary: Conway-era governance gave ADA holders real on-chain power, but the context needed to use it well is scattered across forums, portals, threads and PDFs.

items.name: Governance actions are hard to understand without deep technical context
DRep rationales are scattered and rarely preserved
Voters react to timelines instead of reasoning from evidence
Constitutional context is hard to connect to live actions
Proposal dependencies and history are easily lost
Treasury outcomes are rarely linked back to delivery

sections.title: Who ratifies what — Cardano's seven governance action types
sections.summary: Each governance action type requires a different combination of voting bodies: DReps, SPOs and the Constitutional Committee.

items.name: Info action
items.desc: No on-chain effect.

sections.title: From idea to enactment — the governance action lifecycle
sections.summary: Every action follows the same on-chain path; the governance layer is to track each step and keep the context attached to it.

items.name: 1. Propose
items.desc: Submitted on-chain with a deposit and CIP-100/108 metadata.

items.name: 2. Discuss
items.desc: Community review; rationales and risk analysis gather.

items.name: 3. Vote
items.desc: DReps, SPOs and the CC cast votes across the epoch window.

items.name: 4. Ratify
items.desc: If the required thresholds are met, the action is ratified.

items.name: 5. Enact
items.desc: Applied in the next epoch; the deposit is returned.

sections.title: Establishing a shared governance roadmap
sections.summary: Beyond tracking individual actions, the governance layer is to help the community propose, prioritise, track and remember governance priorities. It rolls out in five phases, mapped to the 4Cs.

items.name: Phase 1 — Connect
items.desc: Index DReps, SPOs and the Constitutional Committee. Mirror live governance actions with neutral, plain-language explainers.

items.name: Phase 2 — Understand
items.desc: Attach constitutional context, risk analysis, dependency maps and clear voting timelines to every action.

items.name: Phase 3 — Participate
items.desc: Calm digests and 'what changed?' views, discussion spaces, and local governance groups — informed participation without the noise.

items.name: Phase 4 — Remember
items.desc: A durable rationale archive, voting history, and proposal-to-delivery evidence.

items.name: Phase 5 — Roadmap
items.desc: A community-curated, living governance roadmap: propose priorities, track progress across epochs, and open the schemas so anyone can build on the governance context graph.

sections.title: Governance memory — so the ecosystem remembers
sections.summary: Governance loses its memory fastest of all — why a decision was made, what was promised, what was delivered. The governance layer is to preserve it as linked, verifiable context.

items.name: Rationale archive
items.desc: Every DRep and CC rationale, kept and searchable — not lost to a timeline.

items.name: Voting history
items.desc: How bodies and individuals voted over time, with the context that shaped it.

items.name: Proposal-to-delivery
items.desc: Treasury actions linked to milestones and on-chain evidence of delivery.

items.name: Decision provenance
items.desc: The debates and dependencies behind a decision, preserved for the future.

sections.title: Treasury proposal at a glance (draft)
sections.summary: A Conway-era Treasury Withdrawal request to deliver the cardano.nexus MVP — open-source, forkable, with every milestone evidenced on-chain.

sections.title: What the proposal funds
sections.summary: ₳350,000 to deliver the Minimum Viable Version across four milestones over roughly six months: an open ecosystem directory, identity profiles, a DRep and SPO directory, a learning resource library, a contribution-needs board, verified links, basic trust signals, a community-submitted ecosystem map, and a public API. Delivered open-source (Apache-2.0) with open schemas; funds released milestone-by-milestone against published acceptance criteria, each completed milestone evidenced on-chain. Success test: can someone arrive at cardano.nexus and understand the Cardano ecosystem better than before?

sections.title: The problem it addresses
sections.summary: Cardano has the technical foundation — a public chain, native assets, wallets, identity primitives, governance, and a global community. What's missing is the human, social and contextual layer. Information is scattered across X, Discord, GitHub, forums, governance portals and meetups, and that fragmentation produces recurring, costly problems.

items.name: People don't know who is building what
Newcomers don't know where to start
Builders repeat work because prior work is hard to find
Trust is built socially but not represented clearly
Ecosystem memory is weak; coordination relies on personal networks

sections.title: Milestones & timeline
sections.summary: Each milestone has explicit acceptance criteria. Funds are released only on verified completion, and completion is anchored on-chain as proposal-to-delivery evidence.

items.name: M1 — Foundations
items.desc: Public repo live; design system shipped; wallet sign-in and profile/identity schemas working on mainnet; chain provider operational with failover.
items.acceptance: A user can sign in with a wallet and create a verified profile.

items.name: M2 — Directory & Context
items.desc: Project / org directory, categories & tags, DRep and SPO directories, and the community-submitted ecosystem map are live and seeded with public data.
items.acceptance: ≥250 profiles and a browsable ecosystem map.

items.name: M3 — Contribution & Trust
items.desc: Update feed, contribution-needs board, verified domain links, and basic trust signals shipped.
items.acceptance: Projects can post needs and verify a domain; trust signals render on profiles.

items.name: M4 — API, Learning & Launch
items.desc: Public API and open schemas published; learning library and docs live; A2A AgentCard served; security review complete; public beta launched.
items.acceptance: Third parties can query the open API; public beta is live.

sections.title: Constitutional alignment — why it fits Cardano
sections.summary: cardano.nexus inherits the values of Cardano itself and respects the constitutional guardrails for treasury spend.

items.name: Public good, not private capture
items.desc: Open-source and open-data; no single operator can own the ecosystem's shared context.

items.name: Neutral & permissionless
items.desc: Does not favour any project, sell visibility, or decide who belongs.

items.name: Strengthens governance
items.desc: Gives DReps and ADA holders shared context — without telling anyone how to vote.

items.name: Accountable spend
items.desc: Milestone-gated release, on-chain delivery evidence, full public reporting.

sections.title: Risks & mitigations
sections.summary: Key delivery risks and how the proposal mitigates them.

items.name: Scope creep
items.desc: Fixed MVP scope with milestone gating; out-of-scope ideas are logged for a future round, not added mid-delivery.

items.name: Low adoption
items.desc: A directory is only useful if populated; seed with existing public data and partner with active communities before launch.

items.name: Centralisation drift
items.desc: A connection layer could become a chokepoint; open schemas, forkability, and a path to progressive decentralisation.

items.name: Key-person / delivery risk
items.desc: Dependence on a small team; open-source from day one, documented build, milestone-based payment so unspent funds are returnable.

sections.title: The ask
sections.summary: ₳350,000 from the Cardano Treasury via a Treasury Withdrawal governance action, released across four milestones to a community-controlled multisig, with all deliverables open-source and each milestone's completion evidenced on-chain. A refundable governance-action deposit (protocol parameter) is locked on submission and returned to the stake address on enactment or expiry. Figures, addresses and the governance action ID are placeholders to be finalised before submission; this is a draft for community review, not financial or legal advice.
